title: feat(spec)!: a controlled_by_parent object derives its master from exactly one required master_detail; the runtime's fallback tiers retire (#23100)
body:
Fixes #23100
Clause-②: no (narrowing)

## What this does

Ruling `6134079470` (batch #331 item 4, letter **B**) enforces ADR-0055 §1: a `controlled_by_parent` object derives its master from **exactly one `master_detail` field declared `required: true`**. Before this PR the parse, the linter and the runtime gave three different answers. They now apply that one rule, and each seam keeps its own read of it.

| seam | before | after |
|---|---|---|
| **parse** — `ObjectSchema` (`packages/spec/src/data/object.zod.ts`) | accepted a `controlled_by_parent` object with no master, with a non-required `master_detail`, with a required `lookup`, or with two masters | `refuseControlledByParentWithoutOneMaster` in `ObjectSchemaBase`'s superRefine refuses all four shapes. It names the object and ADR-0055 §1. Zero masters are reported at `sharingModel`, and the message names each field that relied on a retired tier. Two or more are reported at `fields`. It applies to raw `.parse()`/`.safeParse()`, `create()`, `defineStack`, `os validate` and the save door. |
| **lint** — `packages/lint/src/validate-security-posture.ts` | `CBP_TIERS`, a three-tier table "mirroring the runtime's winner, exactly" | One predicate, `cbpMasterCandidates`. The no-relation rule fires on zero candidates. The ambiguity rule fires on two or more, and its verdict is now "no master is derived": it no longer names a winner by field order. The `os explain` entries are rewritten to match. |
| **runtime** — `resolveCbpRelation` (`packages/plugins/plugin-security/src/security-plugin.ts`) | `pick(required master_detail) ?? pick(any master_detail) ?? pick(required lookup)`, first by field order | Exactly one required `master_detail` that has a reference resolves. Anything else resolves `null`, which is fail-closed: reads get `RLS_DENY_FILTER`, writes get `422 INVALID_METADATA`. A new `reportCbpMasterUnresolved` warns once per object per cache generation and names the shape the object relied on. The reference-**spelling** tolerance in the same reader is a separate, deliberate decision and is unchanged. |

### ADR-0087 disposition: refused loudly, not converted

- **Disposition.** It is `registered cbp-master-relation-tiers-retired`, a new step-18 D3 semantic entry. There is no D2 conversion, because neither retired shape maps losslessly.
  - Turning a `lookup` into a `master_detail` changes what deleting the master does to every row.
  - Leaving `controlled_by_parent` is the author's call, per the ruling's fork clause.
- **Stored rows.** `applyConversionsToStoredItem` finds nothing to convert. The row then fails `ObjectSchema` and is still registered under its `[metadata_spec_invalid]` diagnostic, which carries the parse's message. The runtime then denies the object and reports it once. No tier is left silently live anywhere.
- **Sibling entries.** The two step-18 entries on the same surface (`cbp-master-detail-required-forced`, `cbp-master-detail-required-lint-error`) are amended in place. Their "raw parse stays tolerant" and "the runtime keeps resolving the master" sentences would otherwise contradict this step inside the same unreleased major.

### HotCRM: measured, not edited

These are read-only readings of the clone at `0f84c9c`. No hotcrm card is filed here, per the ruling.

| object | relation today | refused by this rule |
|---|---|---|
| `crm_campaign_member` | `crm_campaign: Field.lookup(..., { required: true })`, no `master_detail` | **yes** (tier 3) |
| `crm_event_attendee` | `crm_event: Field.lookup(..., { required: true })`, no `master_detail` | **yes** (tier 3) |
| `crm_article_feedback` | `crm_knowledge_article: Field.lookup(..., { required: true, deleteBehavior: 'cascade' })`, no `master_detail` | **yes** (tier 3) |
| `crm_contract`, `crm_quote`, `crm_quote_line_item`, `crm_opportunity_line_item`, `crm_contact` | one `Field.masterDetail(..., { required: true })` each | no |

The changeset's FROM → TO names the three objects. For `crm_campaign_member` and `crm_event_attendee` it prescribes `deleteBehavior: 'restrict'`. Both objects document today's behaviour on purpose: a campaign or event that still has members or attendees cannot be deleted. A plain `master_detail` would cascade instead. `crm_article_feedback` already cascades.

### Fixture triage (the three dispositions)

| fixture | disposition |
|---|---|
| `spec` `object.test.ts`: "forces EVERY master_detail reference" | **replaced**. It pinned that nothing enforced the count, and now pins the two-master refusal. |
| `spec` `object.test.ts`: "raw .parse() stays TOLERANT" | **replaced**. It is now the refusal, with the stored body still unrewritten. |
| `lint` posture tests: step-2 and step-3 silent controls, tier-2/3 ties, "names the OTHER field as the winner", the #22212 lookup-child warning | **replaced**. Each is reversed into the retired-tier refusal. |
| `lint` `validate-expressions.test.ts`: master-detail count fixture | **re-spelled**. It used `controlled_by_parent` incidentally and now uses `private`. |
| `verify` `parent-write-reach.test.ts`: every `controlled_by_parent` fixture's `master_detail` | **declaration added** (`required: true`). These fixtures were never §1-legal: through `defineStack` they ran on tier 2. `pwr_two_masters` and `pwr_no_master` are now excluded by the parse's own refusal. |
| `plugin-security` `controlled-by-parent-sharing.test.ts`: the tier-2 row of the 422 `MISSING_REQUIRED_FIELD` `it.each`, and the required-lookup case | **replaced**. Both move into a new retired-tier block (below). |

### In-flight coupling

- **#23114 (#23093).** It landed on `main` while this was in flight and has been merged in. Its fixtures in `controlled-by-parent-chain-middle-master.test.ts` are tier 1. Its hunks in `packages/verify/src/parent-write-reach.test.ts` (around `:240`–`:285`) and this PR's (around `:60`–`:180`, plus the controls fixture near `:309`) merged without conflict. Before this PR, the verify fixtures it relies on (`pwr_quote`, `pwr_quote_line`) resolved through tier 2.
- **#22900.** It landed too. Its boot and registration regions are not touched here.

## Pins (one refusal and one accepted control per seam)

- **Parse** (`packages/spec/src/data/object.test.ts`): the accepted control covers raw parse, builder and lookups beside the master. The refusals cover the required lookup (parse and builder), the non-required `master_detail` (omitted and `false`), no relation, two masters, and other sharing models left alone. `defineStack` is covered both ways.
- **Lint** (`packages/lint/src/validate-security-posture.test.ts`): each rule's control and its refusals. A new `it.each` holds the lint's verdict equal to the parse's on five shapes. The accepted shape is asserted to parse whole, so the refusals come from this rule rather than from a refinement that never ran.
- **Runtime** (`packages/plugins/plugin-security/src/controlled-by-parent-sharing.test.ts`, block "the retired master tiers derive NO master"): the accepted control reads rows, reaches the executor and reports nothing. Each retired shape (non-required `master_detail`, required `lookup`, two masters) is checked for all of the following:
  - reads denied on both the middleware face and the analytics face;
  - the by-id update and the insert answer `422 INVALID_METADATA`;
  - the report fires exactly once;
  - the parse refuses the same schema at the same path.

## Verification

Readings are at three trees. **`ba6686ce6`** is the final head: `main` at `02bec6ca8` merged in. **`7ed362fd2`** is the same diff before that merge; the only difference is 7 `main` commits that touch none of this PR's files. **`b17a2e120`** is the first merge of `main`, before one verify-test commit. Every exit code was captured before any pipe.

- 126 exited 0.

**Suites.**

| package | tree | files / tests |
|---|---|---|
| `@objectstack/spec` | `b17a2e120` | 660 / 20027 pass (1 todo) |
| `@objectstack/spec` targeted (`object.test.ts`, migrations, error-catalog docs, step-18 merge) | `ba6686ce6` | 7 / 468 |

`typecheck` exited 0 for `spec`, `lint` and `plugin-security` at `b17a2e120`, and for `verify` at `ba6686ce6`. Each printed its `check:test-typecheck: OK` line. Every suite ran on a rebuilt dependency closure (`turbo run build --filter=…^...`).

The sweep direction is downstream: the consumers of `@objectstack/spec` that hold `controlled_by_parent` fixtures or seeded objects. `turbo ls --affected` was not used to narrow anything here.

**Census.** At `b17a2e120`, all 115 authored `*.object.ts` files outside tests and fixtures were imported through the built spec, so `ObjectSchema.create()` ran the new rule at module load. There were 0 import failures. Of 120 objects, 3 are `controlled_by_parent`: `crm_opportunity_line_item`, `showcase_expense_line` and `showcase_invoice_line`. Each has one required `master_detail` and parses. The CLI eval corpus adds 4 more `controlled_by_parent` objects, and the rule refuses none of them. A tier-3 control object was refused, which proves the census can see a refusal.

**Ablation (reverse verification).** The fix was committed first. Each mutation went through `scripts/ablation-replace.mjs` in WRAP mode, which checks the anchor hit and the blob change on disk and restores with `git checkout HEAD`. Both subjects import from `src/` (relative imports), so no `dist/` leg applies.
- **Parse.** Deleting the `refuseControlledByParentWithoutOneMaster(...)` call (anchor 1 → 0, call sites on disk 0) failed **6 / 205** in `object.test.ts`: every refusal pin. The accepted control and the "other sharing models" pin stayed green, as predicted.
- **Runtime.** Putting the three-tier ladder back into `resolveCbpRelation` (marker on disk 1, anchor 0) failed **3 / 36** in `controlled-by-parent-sharing.test.ts`: the three retired-tier cases. The control and the no-master-detail 422 stayed green, as predicted.
- **Restores.** Both were proven: the blob equals HEAD (`1f74c94d8fd6`, `ffac0c727d4f`) and `git diff HEAD` is empty.

**ESLint (a declared narrowing).** `eslint --no-inline-config --format json` over the 15 touched `.ts` files reported 15 files, 0 errors and 0 warnings.
- `--print-config` resolves each of the 15 inside the config.
- The config enables no type-aware linting (`parserOptions` is `{ ecmaVersion, sourceType }` with no `project`), so this diff cannot move a verdict on an untouched file.
- The repo-wide `pnpm lint` is CI's run.

## Acceptance notes (not changed here)

- **`packages/verify/src/parent-write-reach.ts` `masterLinkOf`.** Its zero-master reason ends "a master the runtime would derive through a required lookup is the runtime's own precedence". No input the parse accepts reaches that branch now, and the runtime no longer has that precedence. Its two-master branch also counts every `master_detail`, so one required plus one non-required is still excluded, although the parse and the runtime both derive the required one. Report-line text only. Carrier: none.
- **The same family's `notDerivable` reason.** "the master … cannot be synthesized" is unreachable for a §1-legal detail: its required master reference blocks the detail first. The pinned case now names the detail's own block, which is the same master one hop earlier. Carrier: none.
- **Stale freeze note in `security-plugin.ts`.** The note in `assertControlledByParentWrite` still says "Direction 1 (#9139) has NOT landed". That has been stale since `ace0a5385`, before this PR. Only its first-shape bullet is marked superseded here.
- **`required` reading.** The runtime now reads `required` as `=== true` (it was truthy), matching the lint. A raw-registered object with a non-boolean `required` on its master now fails closed.
- **Object extensions are not judged by this rule.** An `ObjectExtensionSchema` that adds a second required `master_detail` to a `controlled_by_parent` base object is not judged at parse. The runtime fails such a merged object closed and reports it. Not measured beyond reading the code.
- **For whoever files the HotCRM card.** `crm_campaign_member` and `crm_event_attendee` document refusal on delete as the intended behaviour, so `deleteBehavior: 'restrict'` on the new `master_detail` keeps it. The ruling's hotcrm text reads "delete semantics become cascade"; that holds only without `restrict`.
